about: What a handler proves (docs/plan/M2-NEEDS-PROOF.md): each set's needs, in the names of needs.json (a scene object by its SceneObj_ name without the prefix, scene, UserFile, CometScheduler, MarioActor), each with the line that makes it. A set may name an earlier set in 'with'. The kernel checks every need of a set before a handler that proves it runs (LumaCore.holds), so a set that names too much shows as a handler that does not run, never as a wrong proof. gen_types.py writes the sets into luma_functions.json ('guarantees') and the kernel's table; a name the build does not know stops it.

sets.name: system
sets.holds: the game system's files are read: some frames after the game starts, never undone

needs.UserFile: SaveDataHandleSequence::initAfterResourceLoaded (made once the system archive is loaded)

sets.name: stage
sets.holds: a game scene's making is finished (GameSystemSceneController mSceneInitializeDone, after GameScene::initAfterScenarioChosen) and it is not taken down

needs.scene: GameSystemSceneController makes the scene's holder before GameScene::init
needs.MoviePlayerSimple: GameScene::init, when a mod has code (NebulaMods::hasCode): a handler runs only in a mod with code

sets.name: player
sets.holds: a stage, and the player's actor is in its MarioHolder

needs.MarioActor: MarioActor's init sets itself in the MarioHolder (MarioActor.cpp, setMarioActor) when the stage places the player (StageDataHolder::initPlacementMario)
